proposed: Pan-HDAC inhibitors, which are non-selective, have been reported to cause numerous adverse effects in preclinical and clinical evaluations, and the five approved anticancer HDAC inhibitors are all non-selective with various side effects.
why: Dropped off-target toxicity and the claim that this restricts clinical use; quotes give only numerous or various side effects of non-selective inhibitors.

proposed: Tobacco and tobacco smoke contain a complex mixture of over 9500 chemical compounds, and 80 carcinogens have been identified in tobacco smoke.
why: Dropped per-puff framing and the 'more than 60' figure; quote 0 gives over 9500 compounds, quote 1 gives 80 carcinogens in smoke.

proposed: In one study, the population attributable fraction of smoking for lung cancer was estimated at 65%.
why: Dropped 'undisputed', 80 to 90% and other cancer sites. Quote gives a 65% smoking PAF; the lung-cancer setting comes from the record note, not the quote text.

proposed: Epidemiological studies have hardly described a statistically significant cancer increase at radiation doses below 100 mSv, and surveys of exposed groups found radio-induced cancers only above 100 mSv.
why: Replaced 'consistently show no increase' and the 100-200 mSv range with the hedged 100 mSv statements; dropped the 40-60 mSv thresholds, which no quote gives.

proposed: The SCUP action spectrum for ultraviolet-induced skin carcinogenesis has a maximum at 293 nm, and in the UVA region above 340 nm the relative carcinogenicity per J/m2 drops to about 10(-4) of this maximum.
why: Gave the quote's numbers instead of the UVB 280-315 nm and UVA 315-400 nm ranges; dropped albino hairless mice, which the quote does not name.

proposed: Radiation-induced thyroid cancer resembles sporadic papillary thyroid cancer in clinical-pathological features and prognosis, although in irradiated patients the infiltrative subtype of basal cell carcinoma was significantly more frequent.
why: Narrowed the 'same histologic types' claim to thyroid cancer (quote 1) and the subtype difference in basal cell carcinoma (quote 0).

proposed: The linear no-threshold (LNT) model has been challenged, and a shift toward considering hormetic effects at low doses is described as gaining momentum in the scientific community.
why: Dropped atomic bomb survivor derivation, 'mounting evidence' and threshold/adaptive effects; the quote says LNT was challenged and cites hormetic effects at low doses.

proposed: In prostate cancer, the low α/β ratio provides a radiobiological rationale for hypofractionated treatment regimens, that is, higher and fewer fractions.
why: Dropped the numeric 1.5-3.0 Gy range and 'particularly evident' clinical utility; both quotes state only the low α/β rationale for hypofractionation.

proposed: Expression of the beta-HPV 8 E6 protein has been reported to induce genome instability independent of UV exposure, and in cells expressing TERT together with HPV8 E6, continued proliferation comes with genome-destabilizing consequences.
why: Narrowed from papillomavirus early genes to HPV8 E6; dropped continuous expression and impaired homeostasis genes, which no quote states.

proposed: HBV DNA is integrated into the host genome: in the human hepatocellular carcinoma cell line Hep3B, an HBV integrant was cloned and the restriction fragment bearing the virus-host junction was sequenced.
why: Dropped the claim about fragments larger than the HBV genome; quotes describe cloned, sequenced virus-host junction fragments, with Hep3B named in quote 1.

proposed: Lymphomas arising in immunodeficient patients are frequently driven by viruses such as Epstein-Barr virus, although the lack of EBV in a proportion indicates that other pathways are also involved.
why: Replaced latent infection and 'greatly increased risk' with what the quote states: immunodeficiency-associated lymphomas are often EBV-driven, with no risk magnitude given.

proposed: HTLV-1, the first discovered human retrovirus, is the etiologic agent of adult T-cell leukemia, and HTLV-2, isolated shortly afterward, was isolated from a patient with hairy cell leukemia.
why: The quote ties HTLV-1 to adult T-cell leukemia but says only that HTLV-2 was isolated from a hairy cell leukemia patient, so the association for HTLV-2 is not asserted.

proposed: In mice monocolonized with the commensal Escherichia coli NC101, the bacterium promoted invasive carcinoma in azoxymethane-treated Il10-/- mice, and deleting its pks genotoxic island decreased tumor multiplicity and invasion.
why: Dropped 'definitive', colorectal progression and 'direct genotoxic mechanisms'; narrowed to the monocolonized AOM/Il10-/- model and the pks deletion result in the quote.

proposed: Five years after Japan's national H. pylori eradication program began in 2013, no reduction in the annual number of gastric cancers had been observed.
why: The quote reports no observed reduction five years in; dropped 'measurable impacts' and the expectation of effects over decades, which it does not state.

proposed: In a trial with 26.5 years of follow-up, participants receiving H pylori treatment had a lower incidence of gastric cancer than placebo (2.57% vs 4.31%; hazard ratio 0.57).
why: Replaced the 17-year cohort claim and persistence of effects with the 26.5-year treatment versus placebo result in the quote; dropped later cancer development.

proposed: Estrogens may contribute to lung carcinogenesis, especially in the presence of tobacco smoke, through reactive intermediates that damage DNA and steroid hormone receptor signaling that promotes growth.
why: Narrowed from some human cancers to lung carcinogenesis and hedged with 'may', as the quote does; dropped 'tumor promoters' across cancers.

proposed: In one study, smoking was positively associated with the persistence of beta/gamma-HPV (crude odds ratio 4.3, 95% CI 1.9-9.6).
why: Narrowed from HPV infections generally to beta/gamma-HPV persistence and from 'significantly longer, less likely to clear' to an association; no nonsmoker comparison is given. Oral setting is in the note only.

proposed: In a trial of the 9vHPV vaccine, efficacy against high-grade cervical, vulvar, or vaginal disease related to HPV-31, 33, 45, 52, and 58 was 96.7%, and another report gave intention-to-treat vaccine efficacy against all HPV-positive cancers as 100% (95% CI 2 to 100).
why: Dropped 'remarkable success' and 'up to 100%' for pre-approval trials; gave quote 0's 96.7% and quote 1's 100% with its wide interval, without calling either a pre-approval endpoint.

proposed: HPV vaccines are highly effective in preventing infections, with efficacy highest in HPV-naive individuals before sexual debut, and hepatitis B vaccination has proved highly successful in reducing disease burden, the carrier state, and HB-related morbidity and mortality.
why: Replaced 'most successful' and 'near-complete efficacy' with 'highly effective' and 'highly successful' as the quotes word it; the before-exposure point is stated only for HPV.

proposed: Cyclin A1 may primarily function in the control of the germline meiotic cell cycle and additionally in the control of the mitotic cell cycle in some somatic cells.
why: Narrowed to cyclin A1; the quote gives a hedged germline meiotic role plus some somatic mitotic role. Dropped S phase and G2 timing, male-specific expression and cyclin A2.

proposed: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, B-type CDKs prevent re-initiation of replication through multiple overlapping mechanisms, including phosphorylation of the origin recognition complex, downregulation of Cdc6 activity, and nuclear exclusion of the Mcm2-7 complex, and CDK activity also affects Cdc6 degradation and nuclear import.
why: Narrowed to yeast B-type CDKs, which both quotes concern; replaced 'S-CDK' and 'MCM nuclear export' with the quotes' wording; dropped the claim that S-CDK also initiates replication.

proposed: The DNA damage checkpoint system prevents the division of damaged cells, primarily through the G1/S and G2/M checkpoints.
why: The quote names G1/S and G2/M checkpoints as the main routes preventing division of damaged cells; dropped the 'different mechanism', unreplicated DNA and mitotic entry details.

proposed: Cyclin D-CDK4 complexes phosphorylate and inhibit members of the retinoblastoma (RB) protein family, including RB1, and regulate the cell cycle during the G1/S transition.
why: Narrowed to cyclin D-CDK4; quote does not mention Cdk6, the three D-type cyclins or the restriction point.

proposed: Cdk2 acts at the G1-S transition to promote the E2F transcriptional program and the initiation of DNA synthesis.
why: Quote describes CDK2 at G1-S and DNA synthesis initiation; dropped cyclin E partnership, expression later in G1 and the 'required' wording.

proposed: After UV-induced DNA damage, G1 cells readily lost cyclin D1, and in p53-proficient cells subjected to DNA damage, Cdk2 is inactivated by the CDK inhibitor p21.
why: Replaced the claimed cyclin D then cyclin E-CDK2 sequence with the two separate findings: cyclin D1 loss after UV damage and p21-mediated Cdk2 inactivation. No order or cyclin E is stated.

proposed: p16 (CDKN2A) acts as a negative regulator of proliferation by interacting strongly with CDK4 and CDK6, which inhibits their ability to interact with cyclins D and to phosphorylate the retinoblastoma protein.
why: Narrowed to p16 inhibiting CDK4/CDK6-cyclin D; dropped p21, p15 and induction through the MAPK pathway, which the quote does not cover. p16 is named in the record note.

proposed: p53 activates transcription of genes, one of which is an inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases, and in response to DNA damage p53 prevents CDK7 kinase activity when associated with the CAK complex, thus stopping cell cycle progression.
why: The quotes do not name p21 or rapid induction of p53; they state that p53 activates a CDK inhibitor gene and, after DNA damage, prevents CDK7 activity.

proposed: Mdm2 is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that mediates ubiquitination of p53, leading to its degradation by the proteasome.
why: Dropped 'obligatory'; the quote says Mdm2 ubiquitinates p53 leading to degradation but not that the interaction is required.

proposed: The p53 protein is a multifunctional transcription factor that induces cell cycle arrest, DNA repair or apoptosis upon binding to its target DNA sequence.
why: Kept DNA repair, which the quote names; dropped differentiation, senescence and angiogenesis and added the arrest and apoptosis functions the quote states.

proposed: L-myc (MYCL1) has been found to be involved in small-cell lung carcinoma.
why: The quote says MYCL1 is involved in small-cell lung carcinoma; dropped discovery through amplification and the neuroendocrine description, which it does not state.

proposed: Amplification of the MYC family member N-myc (MYCN) is found in about 25% of neuroblastoma cases and correlates with high-risk disease and poor prognosis.
why: Replaced how N-myc was discovered with the quote's amplification frequency and prognosis. The quote itself does not name neuroblastoma; that comes from the record note.

proposed: The MYC oncogene is a potent driver of growth and proliferation but also sensitises cells to apoptosis, and upon aberrant oncogene activation normal cells can enter senescence, a state of stable cell-cycle arrest.
why: Narrowed to Myc for apoptosis (quote 0) and to oncogenes generally for arrest via senescence (quote 1); dropped Ras and 'most normal cells'.

proposed: The occurrence of mutations in genomic stability genes that lead to an increased cellular mutation rate (the mutator phenotype) is presumed to be a primary event in oncogenesis, and many investigators favor the hypothesis that a mutator phenotype is necessary for a single cell to acquire the multiple genetic changes found in cancer.
why: Replaced the carcinogen exposure, clonal selection and decades-long timeline, which no quote states, with the hedged mutator phenotype statements in quotes 0 and 1.

proposed: Recent work in animal models suggests that extra centrosomes can accelerate tumourigenesis in the absence of the tumour suppressor p53.
why: Replaced p53 loss causing instability and aneuploidy with the quote's finding that extra centrosomes accelerate tumours when p53 is absent, in animal models.

proposed: Combined treatment with radiation and inhibitors of checkpoint kinases such as Chk1 results in checkpoint abrogation and mitotic catastrophe, which might selectively radiosensitize tumor cells that often lack the p53-dependent G1 checkpoint and rely more on the G2 checkpoint.
why: Added the radiation combination and 'might' from the quote; dropped the claim that Chk1 inhibitors specifically force p53-deficient cells through G2. The quote says 'these kinases'; Chk1 is from the record note.

proposed: The ATR-Chk1 pathway is the principal direct effector of the DNA damage and replication checkpoints, which arrest cell cycle progression upon DNA damage or upon DNA replication stalling.
why: Quotes describe the ATR-Chk1 pathway and checkpoints responding to replication stalling; neither mentions ATR inhibitors, so the inhibitor-targeting claim is dropped.

proposed: CDK4/6 inhibitors have been tested in combination with other drugs in clinical trials, including a Phase Ib/II study of ceritinib with the CDK4/6 inhibitor LEE011 in ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer.
why: Dropped 'validated the cell cycle as a therapeutic target' and the claim of new avenues; the quotes show only trial registrations in lung cancer and melanoma, not success. Melanoma trial omitted as it does not name a CDK4/6 inhibitor.

proposed: WEE1 is a serine/threonine kinase that regulates the G2/M checkpoint by phosphorylating CDK1, preventing premature mitotic entry, and in one study the effects of MK-1775 were strongly elicited by apoptosis and lethal mitosis but less likely by abrogation of radiation-induced G2 arrest.
why: Quote 0 gives WEE1's inhibitory phosphorylation of CDK1; quote 1 tempers the claim that MK-1775 acts by preventing G2 arrest. Adavosertib blocking the phosphorylation is not stated.

proposed: Centrosome amplification, observed in various solid tumors, contributes to chromosomal instability and poor clinical prognosis, and could participate in tumour progression through chromosome instability, disruption of tissue architecture and promoting cell invasion.
why: Hedged to 'contributes' and 'could'; dropped abnormal chromosome number, hallmark-of-cancer status and therapeutic targets, which neither quote states.

proposed: Application of a method to somatic mutations of more than 28,000 tumours of 66 cancer types has revealed 568 cancer genes and points towards their mechanisms of tumorigenesis.
why: Replaced 'about 100' viral and cellular oncogenes with the quote's different figure of 568 cancer genes; the quote concerns somatic mutations, not viral oncogenes.

proposed: Large-scale cancer genome sequencing studies have revealed that chromatin regulators are frequently mutated in cancer, and more than 20% of cancers harbour mutations in genes encoding subunits of SWI/SNF (BAF) chromatin remodelling complexes.
why: Replaced 'among the most frequently mutated' with 'frequently mutated' and named chromatin regulators and SWI/SNF as the quote does; no ranking is stated.

proposed: Acquired resistance to cell death is a hallmark of cancer, and defects in the control of apoptosis promote the development of cancer and its resistance to therapy.
why: Quote 0 states resistance to cell death is a hallmark; quote 1 says apoptosis-control defects promote development and therapy resistance. Dropped 'critical step' and 'fundamental'.

proposed: Paul Ehrlich, who received the Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine, has been called the founder of chemotherapy.
why: The quote calls Ehrlich the founder of chemotherapy and notes his Nobel Prize; coining the term, nationality, infectious disease work and animal screening are not stated.

proposed: In one study, the cumulative incidence of grade 3-5 chronic health conditions at age 50 was 96.0% in survivors, and late effects after childhood cancer treatment occur in over two thirds of patients 30 years after the end of treatment.
why: Replaced 'more than 40 percent within 30 years of diagnosis' with the quotes' figures: 96.0% severe (grade 3-5) conditions at age 50 and over two thirds with late effects 30 years after treatment.

proposed: In one study, moderate-to-severe hearing loss, a late effect of treatment, was identified in 72% (236 of 327) of participants.
why: Quote gives one late effect (hearing loss) in 72% of participants; the 'two-thirds of survivors' share, the definition and the five-year window are not stated. Neuroblastoma survivors are named only in the note.

proposed: Risk factors for posttreatment fatigue include the presence of pretreatment fatigue, which significantly predicted post-treatment fatigue, and greater body mass index, which was significantly associated with moderate to severe fatigue.
why: Kept pretreatment fatigue (quote 0) and body mass index (quote 1); dropped the type of cancer treatment, which neither quote supports.

proposed: Ki-67 is a nuclear protein found in the chromosome, nucleus and nucleolus.
why: The quote gives only subcellular location; dropped expression in G1, S, G2 and M phases and absence in G0, which no quote states.

proposed: A mouse model is described in which introduction of a p53 mutation prevents senescence, accelerates tumor formation, and increases medulloblastoma incidence.
why: Dropped 'all' mice and the quoted endpoint; the quote says p53 mutation increases medulloblastoma incidence, with no per-genotype figure. Ptch1+/- background is from the note.

proposed: Broadly speaking, a chemically induced mouse model can reproduce hepatocellular carcinoma that arises in association with advanced liver fibrosis.
why: Narrowed from chemically induced models in general to one mouse model of HCC with advanced fibrosis; the quote does not state human liver-damage-triggered tumorigenesis or general suitability. Chemical induction is from the note.

proposed: Photosensitivity reactions after the injection of verteporfin are listed among adverse events occurring in 1%-10% of patients, and any exposed person must be protected from bright light.
why: Replaced 'quite common' with the label's 1%-10% frequency band; the second quote adds the light-protection warning without a frequency.

proposed: In one study, fractionated schedules that showed a trend for increased cure were six fractions of superficial illumination with short (1 h) dark periods, and for mTHPC-mediated PDT, discontinuous illumination with 30 s light and dark periods improved the tumor response further.
why: Reversed the claim that intervals of hours are ineffective: quote 0 shows a trend for increased cure with 1 h dark periods; quote 1 shows benefit with 30 s periods. Repair mechanisms are not mentioned.

proposed: One meta-analysis found that depression was associated with cancer recurrence [1.24 (1.07, 1.43)], all-cause mortality [1.30 (1.23, 1.36)] and cancer-specific mortality [1.29 (1.11, 1.49)].
why: Replaced the 50-study hazard ratio of 1.34 and four cancer types with the quote's figures; the quote does not name the cancer types, so they are dropped.

proposed: In one study, anxiety levels and quality of life were similar among childhood cancer survivors, their siblings, and their peers.
why: Quote contradicts the twofold-risk claim for adult survivors: it reports similar anxiety among childhood cancer survivors, siblings and peers; depression and psychological symptoms are not covered.

proposed: Positive outcomes were found with cognitive behavioral therapy and mindfulness-based programs, which led to improvements in cancer-related fatigue, and with mindfulness-based stress reduction, which reduced subjective but not objective memory-related impairments in breast cancer survivors who received chemotherapy.
why: Dropped psycho-education and relaxation, which no quote covers; kept CBT and mindfulness-based programs (quote 0) and MBSR for subjective memory only (quote 1).

proposed: A guideline states that the prevalence of anxiety and depression is higher in patients with cancer than in the general population, though this is often underrecognised.
why: Dropped 'significantly greater'; the quote says only 'a higher prevalence'. Anxiety and depression as the conditions come from the record note, not the quote text.

proposed: The factors associated with worse FT in one study were younger age, lower earnings at diagnosis, and loss in earnings.
why: Kept only younger age and lower income, which quote 0 supports, and added loss in earnings; dropped being female, adjuvant therapies, recent diagnosis and 'most commonly reported'.

proposed: Caregivers of cancer patients are at greater risk of developing depression than the general population, and one review found a pooled prevalence of depression among caregivers of cancer patients of 42.08%.
why: Quotes compare caregivers with the general population, not with caregivers of other patients, and cover depression only; anxiety is dropped.

proposed: In one study, patient-reported outcomes and physical fitness variables remained significantly improved compared with baseline in the exercise group at 3-month follow-up.
why: Quote 1 shows fitness and patient-reported outcomes still improved at 3 months; it does not report physical activity levels, so 'modest increases in physical activity' and 'existing interventions' are dropped.

proposed: In one study, 92% of 163 patients had at least one physical impairment, and 469 (88%) of the 530 identified impairments required physical therapy and/or occupational therapy.
why: Matches the 163 patients and 530 impairments, but the quote does not say the impairments went undetected during hospitalization or name metastatic breast cancer, so both are dropped.

proposed: In China, the incidence of westernized lifestyle-related cancers (colorectal, prostate, and bladder cancer) has risen from 2000 to 2011, while the incidence of the digestive cancers has decreased.
why: Narrowed from countries transitioning generally to China; dropped 'clearly underway' and the claim that falling infection-related cancers are offset by rises, which the quote does not state.

proposed: The majority of colorectal cancer is sporadic and largely attributable to modifiable environmental risk factors characterizing westernization, although another study suggests that only a third of the variation in cancer risk among tissues is attributable to environmental factors or inherited predispositions.
why: Narrowed from 'more than 90% of cancers' to colorectal cancer, where quote 0 says the majority are attributable to modifiable factors; quote 1 tempers the claim. No 90% figure or 'largely preventable' is stated.
